_note: Mechanism: bad system. Analogue habits bolted onto digital work, defended as rigour. Ends on the loop closing on itself.

premise.situation: A colleague prints out emails in order to read them properly
premise.turn: He annotates them by hand, types the annotations into a reply, and prints the reply

character_sheet: a man in his fifties, reading glasses on a chain, short-sleeved shirt

beats.text: There is a man in accounts who prints out his emails.
Not to file them. To read them. He says he reads better on paper.
He highlights them. He has a highlighter. For emails.
Then he writes his reply on the paper, by hand, in the margin.
Then he types the margin into an email and sends it.
And I know what happens next, because I have watched him do it.
He prints the reply. For his records.
